e7_s4_rationale: The presence of hyperchromatic and variable in nuclear size tumor cells, scattered mitoses and necrosis, and the diffuse positivity for smooth muscle actin (SMA) along with CD31 immunostain highlighting many endothelial-lined vascular channels are consistent with epithelioid hemangioma.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: While angiosarcoma can present with similar vascular features, the lack of more aggressive histological features and the specific immunohistochemical profile makes it less likely.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma
e7_s4_rejected.why: This entity typically shows a more myoid or spindle cell morphology and lacks the characteristic epithelioid features seen in this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Retiform hemangioendothelioma typically has a retiform or arborizing vascular pattern, which is not described in this case.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Dabska tumor
e7_s4_rejected.why: Dabska tumor is a rare vascular tumor that typically presents in children and has distinctive histological features, including the presence of hobnail endothelial cells, which are not mentioned in this case.
